title: Attach recent HABIT events to the ranker request

chapters.title: Today: four Tardis features
chapters.lead:
Two new threads join in Builder.Build.

flowchart LR F[fetcher]:::added --> B[Build]:::changed P[field 12]:::added --> B click F "rr:code/pkg/features/habit/fetcher.go#L20-28" "the fetcher" click P "rr:code/proto/feed/v2/ranker_request.proto#L15-26" "the proto" click B "rr:code/pkg/ranker/request_builder.go#L42-61" "Build"

steps.text: Before, Builder.Build fetches from Tardis and wraps the result. No event history reaches the ranker.
Four keys: language, city, affinity, 7-day watch time. Unchanged.
Next: the fetcher, then the proto, then where Build joins them.
RecentEvents gives TFS a 30 ms deadline derived from the caller's context, and wraps any error, including the deadline.
habitKeys asks for one key per hour of the window: 168 keys for the 7 days Build passes.
decode keeps the first 50 rows in the order TFS returned them. The doc comment promises newest first; nothing here sorts, so that holds only if TFS returns rows newest first.
A new HabitEvent message: event, post id and a millisecond timestamp.
Field 12 is new and repeated. Its comment is the contract: newest first, at most 50, empty when the fetch degrades.

Full sequence: Request path.

steps.text: The habit call starts only after Tardis.Fetch returns, so its time adds to every request. Its 30 ms deadline starts then too.
The fetcher arrives through Deps, next to the Tardis client and metrics; its comment says the service wiring in cmd/mfas injects it.
Happy path: the events go straight onto field 12, beside the unchanged Tardis features.
On any fetch error the builder logs a warning and sends nil; the request still goes out.
A Tardis error still fails the whole request, as before. Only the habit signal is best-effort.

The whole path: field 12 gets the events, or nil on error.
